title: Preserve NaN values when normalizing in Styler gradients with equal min and max
answers: Why does Styler.background_gradient color NaN as the lowest value when all values are equal?
Why are missing values styled with the minimum colormap color in Styler.background_gradient or text_gradient?
How to prevent matplotlib Normalize from converting NaN to 0 when vmin == vmax in pandas Styler?
Why does Styler gradient ignore missing-value bad color when vmin equals vmax?
body:
Symptom: Styler.background_gradient and Styler.text_gradient color missing/NaN cells with the lowest colormap color instead of the colormap's bad/missing color when all valid values in a slice are equal or vmin == vmax.
Root cause: In pandas/io/formats/style.py:_background_gradient, matplotlib.colors.Normalize maps NaN to 0 when vmin == vmax, so the colormap treats missing values as the minimum scalar instead of NaN.
Fix pattern: Re-mask NaNs on the normalized output using np.where(np.isnan(gmap), np.nan, norm(gmap)) before passing the values to the colormap.
Constraints: Applies when passing arrays with NaNs to matplotlib.colors.Normalize where vmin == vmax can occur; unnecessary when inputs are guaranteed non-NaN or when normalizers preserve NaN.
applies: pandas.io.formats.style._background_gradient and Styler gradient color normalization with matplotlib
